goal: Ship the three send governors that stand between an approved Solicitation batch and a physical send — the platform-wide reputation circuit breaker, the platform daily ceiling, and the account daily cap — as callable domain modules with explicit sql parameters, plus migration 110 (dispatch-time withhold vocabulary, solicitation_outreach.bounce_kind, and the solicitation_send_breaker latch table). Nothing in this feature sends.
non_goals: No sends, no send worker, no release poller, no releaser wiring — that is #899 and #900
No Judge logic, no auto-approval lane (#631), no review_attributed (#632)
No flag flips anywhere — this lands inert behind SOLICITATION_SEND_ENABLED
No resolveSolicitationDailyCap() twin and no DEFAULT_DAILY_SEND_CAP_BUSINESS (both dropped by amendment B3)

No new value for Dispatch gate item 3 (subscriptionGrantsFullAccess) — amendment B14 moves that check from the per-child Dispatch gate to the RELEASE-level gates beside the caps, so no child ever defers on it and no CHECK member is needed; send_window_elapsed still terminalizes. B6 item 3's original placement was wrong: #900 CASes rendered->queued BEFORE the Dispatch gate runs, so a deferring child stranded a queued row the release predicate could never see again
No new runbook file — the ramp table and seed-inbox gate keep their single owner in docs/runbooks/solicitation-sending-domain.md
No backfill of bounce_kind — no send worker exists, so no row in any environment carries sent_at
No per-domain or per-account scoping of the breaker — one database is one Sending identity
user_visible_behavior: A RepWorth admin sees a new Safety-group page /admin/solicitation showing the send circuit breaker state: open or tripped, the tripping metric snapshot, and the 7-day window figures
A RepWorth admin with AAL2 can reset an open trip by supplying a free-text note; the control is absent or inert when no trip is open
The HealthAlertPoller raises an error-level finding when the reputation window breaches, naming the breached metric and its value
No owner-facing behavior changes at all — the governors have no production caller until #900
invariants: Invariant #15: send-breaker and send-cap modules take sql / tx as an explicit parameter and never import @/lib/db/server
Invariant #13: SOLICITATION_PLATFORM_DAILY_CAP stays server-authoritative with no NEXT_PUBLIC_ companion
Invariant #1: the breaker read model and the trip write run on Railway; the Next.js admin route only orchestrates the reset
Invariant #8: the admin reset route is AAL2-gated and the reset actor is fixed by the session identity, never read from the request body
The breaker read path fails CLOSED: a database failure inside readSendBreaker propagates so the caller halts, never degrading to unmeasured-therefore-send
The breaker never self-clears — only an explicit admin reset closes a trip
At most one trip row is open (reset_at IS NULL) at any time, enforced by a partial unique index rather than by application code
Gate order is fixed: breaker then platform ceiling then account cap then per-child (#622 §4.3)
The account cap dial moves toward restraint only: effective cap = LEAST(configured, DEFAULT_DAILY_SEND_CAP_ACCOUNT)
The platform ceiling fails closed: unset or unparseable yields 0, which means no sends; an explicit 0 is the dial at rest
Counting basis for both caps is dispatch attempts — outreach rows whose queued_at falls in the UTC day — never sent_at
solicitation_send_breaker carries deny-all RLS; it is platform-scoped and therefore not a TENANT_TABLES member

Migration 110 is additive only, and the full object list is: one nullable column (bounce_kind) with its two named CHECKs, two new members appended to an existing CHECK's withheld arm, one partial index (idx_solicitation_outreach_sent_at), and one new table with its one-open partial unique index. No data change.
DEFAULT_DAILY_SEND_CAP_ACCOUNT and DEFAULT_DAILY_AUTO_POST_CAP are separately owned constants that coincide at 10 by design and are never derived from one another
edge_cases: Soft bounces stamp bounced_at too, so the hard-bounce rate must read the new bounce_kind column — provider_error prefix matching is masked by recordFailure's COALESCE when email.failed lands before email.bounced
Fewer than 100 sends in the 7-day window never trips the breaker however bad the rate

The numerator is signal-dated (bounced_at / complained_at in window) while the denominator is send-dated (sent_at in window), so the ratio can exceed 1.0 in a pathological burst — that is a trip, not a bug
A second breach while a trip is already open is a no-op, not a constraint error — the trip insert tolerates the one-open partial index

An admin reset while the window is still breached is permitted and does NOT re-trip on the next poller tick: readBreakerWindow bounds every counter at GREATEST(NOW() - 7 days, MAX(reset_at)), so the reset moves the window's lower edge to the reset instant and only post-reset activity is measured. BREAKER_MIN_SENDS then holds the breaker quiet until 100 fresh sends accumulate — a bounded half-open probe, not a blind re-arm. Pre-reset bounces that land late fall outside the new edge and are not counted; that exclusion IS the fix, because before the bound the breaker measured a history no operator action could change and recovery was arithmetically unreachable
The health check runs unconditionally, including when SOLICITATION_SEND_ENABLED is false, because the Solicitation lane records webhook facts regardless (rule DR1)
Worst-case trip latency is one HEALTH_ALERT_POLL_INTERVAL_MS window (5 min default) — bounded and stated, not eliminated
The new health check must join the SEQUENTIAL list in runHealthChecks — a Promise.all peer wedges the max:2 bulkhead client (#505)
The breaker read model is a cross-account aggregate over solicitation_outreach and needs a tenant-scope allowlist entry
A NULL daily_send_cap resolves to the platform default of 10, not to unlimited
The reset route returns 409 when no trip is open, mirroring the unsuspend route's not_suspended arm

The UTC day boundary for the cap count is date_trunc('day', NOW() AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AT TIME ZONE 'UTC' — the TRAILING conversion is load-bearing and is what worker/jobs/response-generation/auto-approval.ts:231 actually spells. Without it the truncated value is a bare timestamp that Postgres casts back to timestamptz using the SESSION zone, i.e. a local-day boundary; an earlier version of this bullet carried the short form and the bug shipped from it once

rollback_plan: Code revert is sufficient and inert: the governors have no production caller until #900 wires them, and the health check is the only live consumer. To back the schema out, apply the reverse in one transaction against staging then prod — DROP TABLE solicitation_send_breaker; DROP INDEX IF EXISTS idx_solicitation_outreach_sent_at (it is on the PRE-EXISTING solicitation_outreach.sent_at, so nothing drops it with the column or the table, and a rollback that forgets it silently leaves 110's only non-O(1) object behind); ALTER TABLE solicitation_outreach DROP COLUMN bounce_kind (which drops solicitation_outreach_bounce_kind_check and solicitation_outreach_bounce_kind_pairing with it — both are named constraints ON that column, so they need no separate statement, but they DO need naming here or a reader cannot tell they were considered); then re-ADD solicitation_outreach_status_reason_consistency with migration 109's CHECK text verbatim. No data migration to reverse: no send worker exists, so no row in any environment carries sent_at or bounce_kind. Migration applies to the staging Supabase project first and to prod in lockstep at promotion. The new-migration skill governs the migration file itself and is invoked before the first line of SQL.
